questions.question: The engineer stated, "I am working on the GERD mega-project today." When converted into reported speech, this becomes: The engineer stated that he was working on the GERD mega-project ______.

options.text: that day
today
the next day
yesterday

questions.explanation: In indirect/reported speech, the time adverb 'today' shifts to 'that day' when reporting past utterances.

questions.question: Cultural heritage and shared historical victories represent intangible assets that unite citizens across generations. What is the closest contextual meaning of 'intangible'?

options.text: Non-physical, abstract, or incapable of being touched
Heavy and constructed of solid concrete
Temporary and legally invalid
Extremely expensive in cash terms

questions.explanation: In Section 7D.1, 'intangible' refers to valuable assets or qualities that lack physical form (such as pride, heritage, or unity).

questions.question: Worku said, "The national athletic team won three gold medals." In reported speech: Worku said that the national athletic team ______ three gold medals.

options.text: had won
wins
has win
will win

questions.explanation: When reporting direct speech in the past, Simple Past verbs ('won') backshift to Past Perfect ('had won').

questions.question: Thousands of enthusiastic citizens decided to ______ in massive numbers to support the national greening initiative.

options.text: turn out
turn down
turn off
turn away

questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'turn out' means to assemble, gather, or attend a public event or mobilization drive.

questions.question: In formal classroom debate evaluation, what term completes the three core criteria of public speaking presentation: Manner, Matter, and ______?

options.text: Method
Memory
Monologue
Mutation

questions.explanation: Section 7B.1 specifies that formal debates are judged on Manner (presentation style), Matter (content and evidence), and Method (logical structure and organization).

questions.question: The commander declared, "We must defend our national sovereignty at all costs." In reported speech: The commander declared that they ______ defend their national sovereignty at all costs.

options.text: had to
must to
ought
shall

questions.explanation: When converting direct speech into reported speech, the modal 'must' expressing obligation backshifts to 'had to'.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that suffers from a VAGUE PRONOUN REFERENCE:

options.text: When the engineer met the project manager, he said that the dam construction was complete.
When the engineer met the project manager, the manager said that the dam construction was complete.
The engineer told the manager that the dam construction was complete.
The project manager announced that the dam construction was complete.

questions.explanation: In Option A, the pronoun 'he' is vague/ambiguous because it could refer to either the engineer or the project manager.

questions.question: According to Section 7C.1 on 'Mega Projects of Countries', how do strategic national infrastructure investments foster national pride and economic transformation?

options.text: By demonstrating national self-reliance, expanding energy capacity, and driving regional economic integration.
By eliminating the need for agriculture or international trade.
By relying entirely on foreign physical labor and grants.
By privatizing all public water resources for personal profit.

questions.explanation: Section 7C.1 explains that landmark national projects (such as GERD) showcase technological capacity, boost self-reliance, and accelerate economic growth.

questions.question: Solve the word relationship analogy based on Section 7D.2: LEGACY is to HERITAGE as MOBILIZATION is to ______.

options.text: assembly
destruction
isolation
stagnation

questions.explanation: 'Legacy' and 'heritage' are synonymous. Similarly, 'mobilization' and 'assembly' (or rally) are synonymous.

questions.question: Select the sentence that is CORRECTLY punctuated according to standard mechanics for direct speech:

options.text: "National pride inspires unity," said the historian, "and it strengthens social cohesion."
"National pride inspires unity" said the historian "and it strengthens social cohesion."
"National pride inspires unity," Said the historian, "And it strengthens social cohesion."
"National pride inspires unity." said the historian, "and it strengthens social cohesion"

questions.explanation: Splitting a direct quote requires commas inside closing quotation marks, lower-case reporting verbs ('said'), and lower-case continuation inside quotes if continuing a single sentence.

questions.question: In the poem 'A Hero Does Not Recognize Death' (Section 7C.2), what central message does the poet convey regarding true heroes?

options.text: A true hero's legacy lives on indefinitely through their noble deeds, art, and sacrifices, transcending physical death.
A hero avoids dangerous situations to prioritize personal physical safety above all.
True heroism is measured strictly by financial riches accumulated in life.
Physical death erases all memory and historical impact of a national leader.

questions.explanation: Section 7C.2 emphasizes that time cannot erase a hero's story; noble deeds and commitment to justice confer enduring historical immortality.

questions.question: The federation official announced: "If our team wins the championship tomorrow, we will host a national celebration." Which reported speech conversion is GRAMMATICALLY CORRECT?

options.text: The federation official announced that if their team won the championship the following day, they would host a national celebration.
The federation official announced that if our team wins the championship tomorrow, we will host a national celebration.
The federation official announced if their team win the championship the next day, they will host a national celebration.
The federation official announced that if their team had won the championship tomorrow, they had hosted a national celebration.

questions.explanation: Converting Conditional Type 1 into reported speech backshifts present 'wins' to past 'won', future 'will' to 'would', pronouns 'our/we' to 'their/they', and 'tomorrow' to 'the following day'.

questions.question: Read the sentence: "In the news report, it says that the new highway project will boost regional trade." Which revision BEST corrects the unattached pronoun reference 'it'?

options.text: The news report states that the new highway project will boost regional trade.
In the news report, they say that the new highway project will boost regional trade.
It is stated by the news report that the highway project will boost trade.
In it, the news report says that regional trade will be boosted by the highway.

questions.explanation: Replacing vague 'it says in...' with a direct concrete noun subject ('The news report states...') eliminates vague pronoun reference.

questions.question: Based on Section 7C.1, what common historical feature links ancient mega-projects (such as the Roman Colosseum) with modern projects like the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD)?

options.text: They represent monumental engineering feats that redefine national infrastructure, foster collective identity, and symbolize economic ambition.
They were constructed without any financial capital or labor.
They served purely ornamental purposes without practical or economic utility.
They were built exclusively for foreign private entities.

questions.explanation: Section 7C.1 highlights that mega-projects serve as symbols of civilizational achievement, unity, and economic progress across different eras.

questions.question:
Reorder the following narrative sentences into a logically coherent paragraph describing an athletic achievement:
(1) Standing atop the podium, she wept tears of joy as the national anthem played.
(2) For years, Abebech had trained relentlessly under the grueling high-altitude sun.
(3) Crossing the finish line ahead of world-class runners, she raised her arms in triumph.
(4) Her dedication finally culminated on the final lap of the Olympic marathon.
questions.explanation: Logical narrative chronological order: (2) Years of prior training -> (4) Culmination on the final lap -> (3) Crossing the finish line -> (1) Podium ceremony with national anthem.
